title: Annotatio II §.III close CONCEPTIO error 1: Fathers twisted toward corporal union ante usum; stop before §.IV
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the Fathers’ sayings recited thus far and very many like them — by which indeed they said the sacred Eucharist consists of a double substance, but understood only of legitimate use, in which those who approach worthily participate not only terrestrial bread but also Celestial; that Eucharistic bread is indeed sanctified by prayers, but with that sanctification by which all other things are, the Apostle witnessing in 1 Tim. 4; that divine virtue and efficacy is poured or infused into the bread by the Holy Spirit, yet only with respect to those who rightly feed on the sacramental bread (inasmuch as they alone, not the bread, are transmuted by power into spiritual power through spiritual participation of Christ’s body) — these sayings of the Fathers, moreover elevated in a Rhetorical style and not to be pressed to Metaphysical rigor, those about to press Consubstantiation have by error drawn thither and interpreted as if the Fathers had inculcated a Corporal Union of bread and Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper even before and outside use, or faithful perception of the bread, about to reconcile and communicate by the work worked, to whoever eats, spiritual virtue — nay the very substance of Christ’s body — in a corporal mode.
pass_b_english: Those Father-sayings meant legitimate use: the worthy receive earthly and celestial; 1 Tim. 4 sanctification; Spirit’s virtue toward communicants, not a changed bread-substance.
Rhetorical, not metaphysical — yet consubstantiation-pressers twist them as if the Fathers taught corporal bread–body union before and outside faithful use, ex opere operato to any eater.
Stop before §.IV (SECOND error — middle-ages Fathers after Chalcedon).
source_text: Itaque recitata hactenus dicta Patrum aliaque similia quàm plurima, quibus equidem Eucharistiam sacram duplici substantia constare illi dixerunt, sed de legitimo tantùm usu intellexerunt, in quo, dignè accedentes, non terrestrem solum panem, sed & Cælestim participant, panem Eucharisticum precibus quidem sanctificari, sed ea sanctificatione, quâ omnia alia, perhibente Apostolo 1. Tim. 4. virtutem quidem ac efficaciam divinam, pani, vel affundi, vel infundi, à Spiritu Sancto, sed respectu duntaxat eorum qui pane sacramentali ritè vescuntur (utpote qui soli, non autem panis, δυνάμει εἰς δύναμιν virtute in virtutem spiritualem, per spiritualem corporis Christi participationem, transmutantur); Hæc inquam dicta Patrum, Rhetoricô præterea elata stylô, nec ad Metaphysicum rigorem exigenda, illuc, per errorem, traxerunt Consubstantiationem enixuri & interpretati sunt, acsi Patres Corporalem Unionem panis & corporis Christi, in Coena Sacra, etiam ante, & extra usum, seu perceptionem panis fidelem, fieri inculcassent, ex opere operato, vescenti cuivis, virtutem spiritualem, quin ipsam corporis Christi substantiam, corporali modo, conciliaturam ac communicaturam.
notes: Twist toward ante usum corporal union; stop §.IV.
